title: Keeping a knife sharp and storing it safely

items.stem: What is the main difference between honing and sharpening a knife?

options.text: Honing removes metal, while sharpening only polishes the blade
Honing straightens the edge, while sharpening grinds off metal
Honing needs a stone, while sharpening needs only a steel
Honing makes a dull edge sharp, while sharpening cleans the blade

items.stem: Your knife has gone dull. What is true about cutting a carrot with it?

options.text: It is safer, since a blunt edge cannot cut skin
It is just as safe, since the grip matters most
It is riskier, since you press harder and it can slip
It is safer, since you cut more slowly with it

items.stem: You cook most days with one knife. Which routine keeps it sharp?

options.text: Sharpen it before every use and never hone it
Hone it once a year and sharpen it every week
Hone it every few uses and sharpen it a few times a year
Do neither, since careful washing keeps it sharp

items.stem: You have just chopped onions. How should you clean the knife properly?

options.text: Put it in the dishwasher with the plates
Leave it soaking in the sink until later
Wipe the blade with a dry towel, using no water
Wash it by hand with soap, then dry it at once

items.stem: Where should you keep a knife between uses so it stays sharp and nobody gets cut?

options.text: Loose in the drawer with the other tools
In a block, in a sheath, or on a magnetic strip
Loose in the sink, so it is ready for washing
On the counter, close to the cutting board
